messages.subject: barplots : need for x axis?
parts:
I can get what I want but can someone possibly explain why some approaches work and some don't?
######################################################################################
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(111)
numbers  <-  sample(1:80, 1000, replace=TRUE)
tt  <-  table(numbers)

# works nicely
barplot(tt)

# does not work
qplot(tt, geom= "bar", stat = "identity")

# does not work
qplot(as.vector(tt), geom = "bar", stat = "identity")

# works nicely
qplot( count, as.vector(tt), geom = "bar", stat = "identity")

#####################################################################################

My main conceptual problem (or duh?) is why does
qplot(as.vector(tt), geom = "bar", stat = "identity")
not work.

I probably am just missing something in the documentation but I just don't see why I need to add an x variable for such a plot. 

Thanks

parts:
>My main conceptual problem (or duh?) is why does
>qplot(as.vector(tt), geom = "bar", stat = "identity")
>not work.

stat_identity with geom_bar requires both x and y but you supply only x.


Actually, in ggplot2 you don't need to count by table:
